chunks: And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār asked Abā al-Ḥasan Mūsā, peace be upon him, about the sick person: may the Jamarāt be stoned on his behalf? He said:
"Yes, he should be carried to the Jamrah, and it should be stoned on his behalf."
I said: "He is not able to do that." So he said: "He should be left in his lodging, and it should be stoned on his behalf."

key_terms.الْجَمْرَةِ: the individual Jamrah where pebbles are thrown
key_terms.الْجِمَارُ: the Jamarāt, the stoning sites in the hajj rituals
key_terms.الْمَرِيضِ: the sick person who is unable to perform the rite personally
key_terms.مَنْزِلِهِ: his lodging or place of stay
key_terms.يُحْمَلْ: he is carried physically to the ritual site
key_terms.يُرْمَى: the act of throwing pebbles in the hajj rite

ai.seo_question: Can the stoning of the Jamarāt be performed on behalf of a sick person during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the rites of hajj for a sick person who cannot perform the stoning of the Jamarāt personally. If possible, he is carried to the Jamrah and the rite is performed on his behalf; if even that is not possible, the stoning may still be performed on his behalf while he remains in his residence.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3006 - Ishaq ibn Ammar asked Abu Al-Hasan Musa (as) about a sick person: Can the stoning of the Jamarat be performed on his behalf?
Imam (as) replied: "Yes, he should be carried to the Jamarat, and the stoning should be done on his behalf."

I said: "What if he is unable to be carried?"
Imam (as) replied: "He may remain in his residence, and the stoning should be performed on his behalf."
